## Virtual mounts (DB-backed, read-only views)

These are generated from database tables / live services rather than real directories on disk:

- **/threads** — conversation history (76 private, 22 background noted in context)
- **/skills** — created skill personas
- **/favorites** — saved model+character presets
- **/tasks** — cron/background job definitions (Autopilot, Dreaming)
- **/uploads** — user-uploaded media (42 items)
- **/searches** — stored web-search results
- **/gens** — generated media (images/video/music artefacts)
- **/ssh** — machine connections + their configured mounts (terminal/SFTP proxy)

## Native storage (real files on the filesystem)

- **/memories** — markdown files, writable
- **/documents** — markdown files + `/documents/templates/`, writable

## Note for the tooling team

`cortex-list` returns identical shapes for both kinds — every entry is `nodeType: "dir"` with `size: null`. There is no `storage`/`mountType` field, so the virtual-vs-native split above is inferred from platform behaviour, not reported by the API. Adding a `mountType: "virtual" | "native"` field would make this answerable from data rather than inference.

All 10 entries returned correctly, paths consistent,no errors.
